In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Fermi-LAT γ-rays are dominated by radio-loud AGNs.

Fermi-LAT γ ray anisotropy (as well as the intensity) is explained by unresolved radio loud active galactic nuclei and the anisotropies of the individual source classes can be used for the identification of their contribution.

Fermi-LAT observations have provided strong evidence for the existence of a large number of unresolved radio-loud AGNs, with their contribution to the γ-ray intensity and anisotropic distribution being the strongest evidence to date.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IGRB anisotropy measured by Fermi-LAT is consistent with that expected from a population of unresolved radio-loud AGNs.
the IGRB anisotropy can be explained by unresolved radio loud AGN.
the Fermi-Lat IGRB anisotropy is consistent with unresolved radio-loud AGNs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Fermi-Lat IGRB intensity, anisotropy measurements, and future predictions are all explained by unresolved radio loud AGN.
unresolved radio-loud AGNs can account for the measured intensity and anisotropic intensity of the IGRBs in the Fermi-Lat energy range.
radio-loud AGNs can account for all of the measured properties of IGRB.
